# Actual support leaves: neutral-response obstruction and a canonical rigidity alternative

This note tests leaf elimination on actual complete lattice families.
It proves a finite first-order criterion, an exact globally optimized
three-fiber obstruction to automatic neutral simplification, and a
bounded rigidity alternative. It does not classify arbitrary critical
circuits or prove OC.

## 1. A leaf defined by the actual anchored constraints

Fix barycentric affine coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_d on R^d and a
finite lattice-complete base P. Write common-normal simplex fibers as

    K_z={lambda_i>=b_i(z)}, r_z=1-sum_i b_i(z)>0.              (1)

For each p consider the finite vertices of the polytope of representations

    t_z>=0, sum_z t_z=1, sum_z t_z z=p, t_p=0.

For each such vertex impose, for every i,

    b_i(p)<=sum_z t_z b_i(z).                                 (2)

If the representation polytope is empty there is no corresponding
inequality. These finitely many constraints are EXACT: all other anchored
inequalities follow by convexity of that representation polytope and by
removing a self coefficient. They are necessary for actual convex fibers.
They are sufficient as well, because the Minkowski sum of the common-
normal simplexes with weights t has lower offsets sum t_z b_i(z), and
(2) puts that simplex inside K_p. Therefore the convex hull of the displayed
fibers has precisely these fibers at every p and no omitted integer base.
Small changes preserving (2) and r_z>0 are genuine compatible variations.

Call one coordinate b_i(p) a **free support leaf** when every inequality
in(2) whose linear form depends on this coordinate is STRICT. This is an
actual support-constraint definition: the coordinate belongs to no active
anchored-contact relation. It is the strongest local kind of removable
leaf, not an arbitrary edge in a chosen graph. Finiteness gives a positive
interval on which changing only this coordinate in either sign preserves
all actual inclusions and positive fibers. The corresponding body velocity
is constant on its one fiber facet and zero on the other facets, apart
from surface-null edges. Thus it belongs to the finite alternative in
`candidate 07dbcd642c33993d`.

A leaf with active contacts requires a simultaneous motion preserving those
contacts and is not automatically free in this sense. No disjointness or
lower-dimensionality of contact cells is assumed.

## 2. The exact regular one-leaf test

Suppose the fixed witness groups have finite REGULAR circuit menus.
For a chosen circuit c at witness i, let W_ic be its actual response
profile and let F be the free-leaf facet of area A>0. Put

    e_ic=(1/A) integral_F W_ic dH_(d-1).

If the outward velocity on F is r and all other facet velocities vanish,
its normalized cover response is exactly

    q_ic'(0)-beta M'(0)=A r(e_ic-beta).                        (3)

This follows from the proper coarea inverse response; the cover shifts
and all-source slack hypotheses are precisely those in the cited finite
alternative. Consequently an outward leaf motion strictly improves all
groups iff every group has some circuit with e_ic<beta. An inward motion
strictly improves all groups iff every group has some circuit with
e_ic>beta. Failure of both tests means there are (possibly different)
groups i_+,i_- satisfying

    min_c e_(i_+,c)>=beta,
    max_c e_(i_-,c)<=beta.                                    (4)

For one witness this forces EVERY available circuit to have e_c=beta.
Thus one-witness stationarity can force exact neutrality, but neutrality
in(3) is ONLY a first-order assertion. Supporting coincidences require
the piecewise-linear inverse q_c from the cited finite alternative;
substituting a freely chosen indicator or allocation into(3) is invalid.

## 3. Actual strict-no-heavy example: both signs of a free leaf raise depth

Let

    T={x>=-1,y>=-1,x+y<=1}, |T|=9/2,
    K_-1=K_1=(3/4)T,
    K_0(t)={x>=-1+t,y>=-1,x+y<=1}.                            (5)

Use exactly the integer bases -1,0,1 and take their actual convex hull.
For all sufficiently small positive and negative t the displayed fibers
are exact: (3/4)T is contained in K_0(t), in particular whenever t<1/4
and t is near zero, and the endpoints are exposed bases. Thus the full
body is convex, has nonempty interior, and has no other integer fibers.

For the barycentric coordinates of T, the endpoint lower offsets are all
1/12 and the middle offsets at t=0 are all zero. The only nontrivial
anchored constraint is the actual midpoint inequality for each coordinate.
All have strict slack1/12. Varying the single coordinate b_1(0)=t/3 is
therefore a free support leaf in the precise sense of Section1.

The actual mixed mass and baseline depth are

    M(t)=153/16-3t+t^2/2,
    beta(0)=Gamma_2=4/9, Q(0)=17/4.                           (6)

The middle volume fraction at zero is8/17<1/2 and each endpoint fraction
is9/34<1/2. All singleton volume quotas and all proper closed-minor volume
quotas relative to the occupied parity budget2 are strict. This remains
true for sufficiently small t. Thus the example is not rescued merely
by adding a no-heavy or proper-minor-count hypothesis.

The complete baseline critical menu at the unique global deepest point
(0,0,0) is the three proper canonical directions (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1),
with integer tilt zero. This is proved in the audited all-normal source
`candidate c4c8ccba329fa548`
and its triangle-cap dependency. Directly, own-fiber Grunbaum and the
paired-centroid-tail theorem give Q(0); the canonical caps attain it and
cover all fibers. In a canonical direction an endpoint pair at opposite
tilts alpha has value4rho^2+alpha^2 while both cuts are proper; outside
that chamber its value is at least(9/2)rho^2>4rho^2. Hence zero tilt is
its only minimum. Every noncanonical middle cap has strictly larger own
mass. The same cap cover makes every nonzero continuous source strictly
shallower, and isolated endpoint-fiber maxima are strictly smaller.

Here is the exact second-order certificate, retaining all normals and the
moving actual global source. Decompose the middle triangle as

    K_0(t)=t h+c(t)T,
    h=(2/3,-1/3), c(t)=1-t/3.                                 (7)

The audited coherent-source theorem gives a smooth actual global maximum
in a neighborhood of (translation,c)=(0,1), with complete cap menu and
all competing fibers controlled. Its normalized translation expansion,
for fixed rho and c, is

    beta(epsilon,c)=4/9
      +[4(h_1^2+h_1 h_2+h_2^2)/(27(c+2rho)^2)]epsilon^2
      +O(epsilon^3).                                         (8)

To justify use along(7), its normal/source implicit-function systems are
smooth in c as well; the compact complementary-normal gap persists on
a small c-neighborhood. Moreover beta(0,c)=4/9 and the first translation
derivative vanishes for EVERY c in that neighborhood. Thus changing c
linearly introduces no extra first-order or mixed second-order term.
At rho=3/4, c=1 and h_1^2+h_1h_2+h_2^2=1/3, (8) gives

    beta(t)=4/9+(16/2025)t^2+O(t^3).                         (9)

Equivalently,

    Q(t)=17/4-(4/3)t+(67/225)t^2+O(t^3).

The positive coefficient in(9) proves that BOTH sufficiently small
nonzero signs of this one-leaf motion strictly INCREASE the true optimized
normalized depth. The first variation is neutral, but there is no finite
neutral simplification along this leaf. The source moves with first
velocity (4/15,-2/15); freezing it at the moving own centroid would give
the wrong optimization problem.

This falsifies the unqualified rule 'a slack support leaf yields descent
or a neutral simplification.' It does NOT falsify a bad-minimum theorem:
the baseline has beta=Gamma_2, above its OC targetGamma_2/2, and has an
affine centroid graph. A valid classification may stop at the alternative
'already in a proved safe class.' That alternative must be explicit.

## 4. A new neutral-response rigidity equation in a bounded canonical stratum

There is a concrete rigidity conclusion when ALL facet-coordinate motions
are free, rather than an unsupported demand that the safe example descend.
Assume d>=2, (1)--(2), and the following actual hypotheses.

* A single selected regular critical circuit uses the d+1 canonical
  vertex-cap directions, with caps

      H_j={lambda_j(x)>=L_j(z)},
      L_j(z)=lambda_j(y)-a_j dot(z-p),

  through one source Y=(p,y). Every cap cuts EVERY fiber properly.
* All caps have the same raw mixed volume Q=beta M. Their actual
  normalized response weights theta_j are positive and sum to one.
* Every individual facet-offset coordinate is two-sided feasible, and
  every normalized first response of this circuit to such a coordinate
  motion is zero.

The last premise follows, for example, at a local minimum when there is
one fixed deepest witness, this regular circuit controls it, and the
exact all-source slack-cover persistence holds. It is not automatic for
several witness groups, where the obstructions in(4) may come from
opposite groups.

Here the coarea normalization is explicit. Use the unscaled continuous
normals u_j=grad lambda_j, whose unique positive dependence is
sum_j u_j=0. Put

    S_j(z)=H_(d-1)(K_z intersect {lambda_j=L_j(z)})/||u_j||,
    S_j=sum_z S_j(z),
    theta_j=(1/S_j)/(sum_h 1/S_h).

Thus a scalar increase of the affine cut threshold removes S_j times
that increment to first order. The theta_j are the ACTUAL quantile
response weights of the selected circuit, not freely chosen probabilities.
Equivalently, with unit normals the circuit coefficients become ||u_j||
and the Euclidean coareas give the same theta_j.

Define the proper relative cap thresholds

    q_j(z)=[L_j(z)-b_j(z)]/r_z,  0<q_j(z)<1.

On facet i, the own cap i is empty. Each other cap j takes the fraction
(1-q_j(z))^(d-1) of that facet: its trace is the homothetic facet simplex
q_j(z) v_j(z)+(1-q_j(z)) F_i(z), where v_j(z) is the opposite vertex
with relative barycentric coordinate j equal to one. Its full-fiber
volume fraction is (1-q_j(z))^d. Neutrality in(3), separately for every
actual facet, therefore gives

    sum_(j!=i) theta_j(1-q_j(z))^(d-1)=beta for all i,z.       (10)

Subtracting two equations and then summing proves

    theta_i(1-q_i(z))^(d-1)=beta/d for all i,z.                (11)

Since d>=2 and the theta_i are fixed positive weights, every q_i(z) is
independent of z. The volume fraction of canonical cap i is then
(1-q_i)^d in EVERY fiber. Equal global cap masses yield

    (1-q_i)^d=beta for every i.

All q_i are consequently equal. At the source p their sum is exactly1,
because sum lambda_j(y)=1 and r_p=1-sum b_j(p). Hence

    q_i=1/(d+1), beta=Gamma_d, theta_i=1/(d+1).                (12)

Finally the barycentric coordinates of the actual centroid g_z are
b_i(z)+r_z/(d+1). By the threshold identity and(12),

    lambda_i(g_z)=b_i(z)+r_z/(d+1)=L_i(z).                    (13)

Every L_i is affine on base space, so the actual centroid graph is affine.
Thus the safe affine-center simplex structure has been DERIVED from
neutrality and the actual equal critical cap masses, not inserted as an
assumption. The free radii may still vary; the conclusion is precisely
about their centroid graph and the normalized critical value.

This excludes a below-target attained minimum in this bounded fully free,
one-witness, all-proper canonical stratum. It does not treat partial
contact cells, arbitrary critical normal directions, supporting facets,
or multiple witness groups. Those restrictions identify the next actual
interfaces instead of renaming their absence a general rigidity theorem.

## 5. A stronger source-facet result and its separate freedom hypothesis

The independently audited source
`candidate 00208e2b45f0da1a`
proves a different, stronger-freedom statement. If the SOURCE simplex
alone permits all independent signed affine facet velocities, and this
one regular canonical circuit is neutral under those motions, then
beta=Gamma_d. For d>=2 its source is the own-fiber centroid and the
response weights are uniform. No all-fibers-proper premise is required.
For d=1 only beta=1/2 follows; the source need not be the interval midpoint.

The additional equations are the facet first moments. After the constant
equations give theta_j(1-q_j)^(d-1)=beta/d, the captured facet centroids
give, for every i,

    sum_(j!=i) q_j(v_j-g_Fi)=0.

Affine independence on each facet forces the claimed source centroid.
This does not replace Section 4: that section uses only facet-CONSTANT
velocities, at all fibers, and concludes an affine centroid graph.

A sufficient ACTUAL two-sided freedom condition for arbitrary small
source-shape changes is strict compact containment in every extreme
anchored Minkowski inclusion involving that source fiber, as input or
target. There are finitely many such inclusions, so a common support
margin survives every sufficiently small Hausdorff perturbation of that
fiber. The root source proves this and the realization of any affine
facet velocity by tilting one actual defining hyperplane. This condition
is not inferred at an arbitrary attained minimum.

The same source proves a useful conditional status alternative. For a
minimal regular circuit, neutrality under every independently feasible
translation of one fiber forces S_j(z)/S_j to be independent of j. Thus
that fiber has positive proper coarea for every cap or for none. This
uses the one-dimensional circuit kernel, not an assumed simultaneous
status rule. Multiple witnesses or supporting coincidences remain
outside this linear-neutrality argument.

## 6. Actual lower-budget menus distinguish the missing premises

There is no universal ordering of the failures. The following exact
examples separate them. Neither is a below-OC example or an asserted
bad minimum. All-normal values and global source control follow from
`candidate f89d52b54ff6950f`,
equations (19)--(20), with the same area-9/2 triangle T as above.

First take radii (a,c,b)=(19/20,1,21/20) at (-1,0,1). The radius is affine,
so all three midpoint support inequalities are EQUALITIES. The canonical
critical caps at the middle centroid have integer coefficient
alpha=a-b=-1/10 and are proper on ALL three fibers. Their raw masses are

    Q=2c^2+(a+b)^2=6,
    M=(9/2)(a^2+c^2+b^2)=5409/400,
    beta=800/1803<4/9.

The two endpoint maxima are 2a^2 and 2b^2, both strictly below 6; the
alternative saturated canonical value 2c^2+(9/2)a^2 exceeds 6. Thus the
proper canonical menu is genuinely globally critical. The three relative
thresholds along each direction are respectively 17/57, 1/3, 23/63.
They do not agree between fibers. Here dependent ACTUAL contacts block
independent facet motions; neither noncanonical normals nor saturation
is needed. The centroid graph is nevertheless affine and the class is
already safe. Strict no-heavy holds since max r_z^2=441/400<601/400.

For a contrasting example take radii (1/5,1,1). Every midpoint support
inclusion is strict, so all single facet-offset coordinates are locally
free. The actual middle depth and total mass are

    Q=2+(9/2)(1/5)^2=109/50,
    M=(9/2)(1/25+1+1)=459/50,
    beta=109/459<4/9.

The largest endpoint maximum is 2<Q. A finite canonical tilt alpha=-3
makes the small left fiber strictly full and the right fiber strictly
empty, while the middle cut is proper. This is an ACTUAL globally
critical regular menu, but the all-proper premise of Section 4 fails.
Moreover its source-facet constant response is 4/9, strictly larger
than beta, so an inward free middle-facet motion supplies a strictly
negative normalized cover response. It is not a neutral local minimum.
This also explains why the stronger source-facet theorem cannot be
applied by omitting its neutrality premise.

These examples locate concrete barriers to the current rigidity lemma.
They do not classify genuinely low-budget attained minima: a proposed
extension must retain active anchored contacts, supporting allocations,
and cross-witness source control rather than declare any one of them
absent from low depth alone.
